intro: The businesses you buy from, kept as a record of their own: who they are, how you reach them, how you pay them, their papers, and everything you have bought and paid. Each supplier's page shows where things stand with them today.
start: Add your main suppliers with New supplier, or bring them all in at once from a spreadsheet with Import and export.
Set how soon you pay each one and the currency they bill in, so bills fall due on the right day.
Add each supplier's bank account and have it verified and approved, so it can be paid.

articles.title: Add a supplier
articles.summary: Record who they are, how to reach them and how you trade, so they can be put on requisitions, orders and bills.

steps.rest: the name you know them by, their registered name and registration number, and a type and category.
a contact person, phone and email.
how many days you pay within, the currency they bill in, and their tax ID, which you need to claim VAT and withhold tax.
Where your settings ask for approval, the button reads Submit for review, and the supplier waits for someone to approve it.

articles.after: A code is given from your numbering if you leave it blank. A bill's due date is counted from the days you pay within.
tips: If it looks like a supplier you already have, Clafina says so. Press View existing to check, or This is a different supplier to go on.
Keep their certificates and licences on the supplier's Compliance tab with Record a certificate. Their expiry dates are watched for you.

articles.title: Add or change a supplier's bank account
articles.summary: An account is paid only when it is active: submitted by one person, verified with the supplier by a second, approved by a third.

steps.rest: and go to the Banking tab.
Enter the account name as the bank holds it, the account number and the currency.
It is submitted. Nothing is paid to it yet.

steps.lead: A second person presses Verify with the supplier
steps.rest: and says how they confirmed it, such as a call to a number you already had. Then they press Mark as verified.
The account is then made active and can be paid.

tips: To change an account, use Change this account. The old one stays paid until the new one is active, and is then retired.
Only the last four digits show. Show the whole number is kept on record each time someone uses it.

articles.title: See what you owe a supplier, or stop buying from them
articles.summary: Read their statement of bills and payments with a running balance, and retire a supplier you no longer use without losing their history.

steps.rest: from Suppliers. The list shows what you owe each one.
and press Show. Their posted bills and payments are listed oldest first, with what is owed at the end.

steps.lead: To stop buying from them, press Retire

tips: Retired suppliers keep their history but are offered on nothing new. Bills and payments already owed still go through; reinstate them to buy from them again.
A supplier no document names can be deleted; one with documents is retired instead.
